drivers.summary: Thombo bureaucracy ties land, status, tax and service into documentary governance.

amplifiers.summary: Registration/codification can strengthen dominant local positions.

constraints.summary: Formal emancipation does not instantly dissolve social dependence.

consequences.summary: Colonial legibility reworks rather than invents hierarchy.

protagonists.name: Colonial administration
protagonists.objective: Make land, people, service and revenue governable.

protagonists.name: Jaffna households and status groups
protagonists.objective: Protect land, status and obligations within changing legal regimes.

what_changed: Hierarchy becomes more legible and documentable to the state.
Legal emancipation and social transformation diverge in tempo.

prepares_next.bullet: The independent state of 1948 inherits a unified administrative machine and unequal access channels whose redistribution will become politically explosive.
